structure_assets.description: Main Figure 1 TEM/HREM/SAED of PVP-L AgNH, not its proposed capping geometry.
Main Figure 2 SEM/TEM/SAED of straight PVP-H fivefold-twinned Ag rods.
Main Figure 3 Z-, V-, d-shaped rods, nanoring, and selected diffraction.
Main Figure 4 AgNH-family seeds before and after electron-beam exposure; panel c is transformed Ag, not as-synthesized seed phase.
Main Figure 5 one-week multipods; later panels show electron-beam decay to FCC Ag, not a separate growth product.
Main Figure 6a author-proposed ideal shape evolution; panels b–c are microscopy. Schematic is not measured atomic geometry.
Main Figure 7 author-proposed inner versus outer PVP capping; conceptual model only.
Main Figure 8 XPS of AgNH, evidence for author capping interpretation, not a ligand-coordinate image.
Main Figure 9 author growth mechanism with exemplar images; arrows and seed pathway are conceptual.
SI Figure S1 additional PVP-H zigzag Ag rods and turning angles.
SI Figure S2a representative newly prepared Ag rod; not the exact rod shown as nanotube in panel b.
SI Figure S2b representative Ag2S nanotube after three weeks in open air; not paired to panel a object.
SI Figure S3 AgNH XRD with decayed FCC Ag reference peaks separately indexed.
SI Figure S4 low/high magnification SEM supporting high AgNH fraction.
Main Figure 4c seed after electron-beam-induced decay to FCC Ag; not as-synthesized seed structure.
Main Figure 5b–d multipod after electron-beam-induced FCC Ag decay; analytical state only.
Main Figure 6b–c SEM shapes in AgNH family; panel a is a separate author-proposed ideal growth diagram.
SI Figure S3 blue-indexed FCC Ag peaks assigned to decayed Ag crystallites, distinct from red AgNH peaks.
Original PVP-H/PVP-L branch map; no measured particle or atomistic geometry.
Original source-bound symbol for High-MW poly(vinyl pyrrolidone); Polymer chain length distribution and adsorption geometry are not measured.
Original source-bound symbol for Low-MW poly(vinyl pyrrolidone); Exact mass for the low-MW branch and internal capping geometry are not independently restated/measured.
Original source-bound symbol for Ambient air, sulfur reactant unidentified; The source assigns an Ag2S nanotube but does not identify the sulfur-donor molecule.

quality.review_scope: Independent scoped scientific quick audit accepted the entire local main PDF pp.1–8 and matched SI pp.1–4 for the packaged PVP-H rod mixture, PVP-L fast AgNH mixture and qualitative slow comparison, one-week multipod extension, open-air Ag2S transformation, electron-beam analytical transformations, and Figures 1–9/S1–S4. Inferred PVP-L charge/hold values, distinct aged and beam-altered products, and author-proposed capping interpretations retain their recorded caveats. Cited upstream Sun/Xia synthesis and earlier AgNH crystal analysis are outside scope.
missing_fields: The PVP-L paragraph does not separately restate AgNO3/PVP-L mass, EG volumes, hot-bath temperature or post-injection hold; inherited rod-route values are explicitly marked inferred.
Exact injection duration for the qualitative PVP-L slow rod branch is not reported.
No isolation/wash sequence for the initial Ag nanocrystal suspensions is reported.
The one-week multipod re-exposure gives no fresh reagent mixture amounts.
Open-air Ag2S nanotube formation has no identified sulfur donor or independent Ag2S crystallographic measurement in SI S2.
PVP inside the AgNH lattice and PVP-H external facet capping are author mechanistic interpretations; no direct molecular coordinates are shown.
Electron-beam dose and yield-counting methods are not reported.
conflicts: Main p.2 says PVP-H does not produce well-defined nanoparticles even at low injection rates while the explicit PVP-H protocol produces defined nanorods. We interpret the comparison narrowly as failure to produce the AgNH-type particles, not as a negation of the rod result.

Main p.7 states 2–3 weeks of open-air Ag rod exposure; SI Figure S2 reports the pictured Ag2S nanotube after 3 weeks. The SI caption explicitly says panel a Ag rod and panel b nanotube are typical different objects.
